Subject: Clarifications: Order Form & Liability Cap (Claraventures RFP)

Hi David,

Thanks for participating in our RFP. Attached is our standard legal questionnaire (Claraventures_RFP_Legal_Questionnaire.pdf). A few items jumped out during our review of the draft order form and exhibit:

1) Liability cap: We expect a commercial cap at 2x fees for SaaS services; your draft proposes a per-claim approach with carrier exceptions. Can you confirm Redwood's position and whether you can accept a 2x fees cap (with carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct)?

2) IP: We need a short confirmation of customer data ownership, and clarity on output/data retention — are outputs considered customer data for IP purposes?

3) Indemnity: We typically require IP infringement indemnity for the model outputs we receive. Please confirm scope and any material exclusions.

4) Order form exhibits: We would prefer minimal back-and-forth; if you can provide a redline of Exhibit B (Order Form) showing any deviations from our template, that will speed procurement.

Can you get answers back by EOD Friday? Procurement is trying to finalize terms before the holidays.

Attachments: Claraventures_RFP_Legal_Questionnaire.pdf (questionnaire, 18 pages)

Best,
Sara Jensen
Sr. Procurement Manager
Clara Ventures

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sara Jensen <sara.jensen@claraventures.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-11T11:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Clarifications: Order Form & Liability Cap (Claraventures RFP)

Hi Sara —

Thanks for the clear list. Please see high-level responses below and attached a filled questionnaire (Redwood_Response_Questionnaire.pdf) plus a clean redline of Exhibit B (ExhibitB_OrderForm_Redline.docx). If you want a tracked-changes Word instead I can upload that.

1) Liability cap: Redwood's standard commercial cap is 2x subscription fees or $5M, whichever is greater. We are willing to accept a 2x fees cap for this engagement, carving out gross negligence and willful misconduct, and limited carve-outs for third-party service failure (e.g., cloud provider outage) where liability is apportioned. Proposed language in the attached redline.

2) IP & data ownership: Customers retain ownership of their input data and any metadata they supply. For model outputs, we grant customers an unrestricted right to use outputs produced for them; Redwood does not claim ownership of customer outputs. We do retain the right to use aggregated, de-identified telemetry for service improvement; we will not use customer-identifiable outputs for model training without an explicit opt-in in the order form (see Section 4 of the attached questionnaire).

3) Indemnity (IP): Redwood provides an IP indemnity limited to: (a) third-party claims that the service as delivered by Redwood infringes a third-party patent, copyright, or trademark, and (b) remedies capped consistent with the liability cap. We exclude indemnity for claims arising from customer-provided prompts or outputs that replicate third-party content (we note this in the questionnaire). We are open to discussing a narrower operational carve-out if Clara can accept our standard exclusion for Open Source model components as noted in Exhibit A.

4) Order form redline: Attached. Key changes are: (i) explicit data residency clause for EU accounts only (we added an option block), (ii) clarified KMS/HSM key ownership options, (iii) versioned SLA windows for Dedicated capacity.

Attachments: Redwood_Response_Questionnaire.pdf (answers, 12 pages); ExhibitB_OrderForm_Redline.docx (redline)

Next steps: If Marissa/Neha are okay with the redline, I can post the updated Exhibit B to the Drive and generate a DocuSign envelope for signature. We can also propose a compromise clause on indemnity carve-outs that limits Redwood's exposure where customers supply model prompts that reproduce third-party content.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — we can hop on a call with procurement/legal if that helps.

Best,

David — thanks for the quick response and redline. A couple quick clarifying items before we escalate to legal: 

> 1) Liability cap: Redwood's standard commercial cap is 2x subscription fees or $5M, whichever is greater. We are willing to accept a 2x fees cap for this engagement, carving out gross negligence and willful misconduct, and limited carve-outs for third-party service failure...

Can you confirm whether the $5M floor applies to our pilot term (initial 6 months) or whether you will prorate the fees calculation? Procurement prefers a prorated calculation based on the committed fees for the first 12 months.

Second, on the IP indemnity: we need to be sure output indemnity covers downstream customer-facing products that embed model outputs. Your note about exclusions for customer-provided prompts is understandable, but we need clarity on how Redwood will handle claims where outputs are substantially similar to a third party's copyrighted content. Are you willing to add a mutual cooperation clause for handling third-party takedowns and a remediation path?

If you can confirm those two points and upload the revised redline, we can move this into legal review.

Thanks —
Mark
Head of Business Ops
Clara Ventures

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Clarifications: Order Form & Liability Cap (Claraventures RFP) — need final legal language

Team — forwarding the latest from Clara (below). Key asks to resolve:

• Prorating the fees calculation for the liability cap for the pilot term (they want prorated first 12 months). Our standard is annualized fees; we should consider conceding prorated for pilot to avoid procurement delays.

• IP/output indemnity: They want clear language that covers downstream products that embed outputs and a mutual cooperation/remediation path for takedown claims. They also want us to clarify the treatment of outputs that substantially replicate third-party copyrighted content.

Proposal for compromise (draft language I'm suggesting for Neha to vet):
- Liability cap: "For the initial pilot term (<=12 months), the liability cap will be calculated based on fees actually invoiced for that period on a prorated basis; thereafter, cap is calculated on annualized fees."
- IP indemnity & cooperation: "Redwood will indemnify Customer for third-party claims to the extent they arise from the Services as delivered by Redwood, subject to the liability cap. If a claim arises from Customer-supplied prompts or content, Customer shall retain primary responsibility; however, Redwood and Customer agree to cooperate in good faith on remediation steps, takedowns, and mitigation. Both parties will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide notice, preserve evidence, and coordinate public statements."

Can you please: (1) confirm whether the prorated liability language is acceptable from a risk standpoint, (2) propose any tightening of the indemnity carve-outs (we'd prefer to keep customer-prompt exclusion but offer cooperation obligations), and (3) if acceptable, produce an updated ExhibitB_OrderForm_Redline_v2.docx and I will send back to Clara with DocuSign link.

Forwarded message included for context.

Thanks —
David
